items.informal_name: Compatibility of Composition with Algebra Evaluation Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  (f : σ → S₁) {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (φ : S₁ →ₐ[R] B),
  φ.comp (MvPolynomial.aeval f) = MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => φ (f i)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $B$ equipped with an $R$-algebra structure and any algebra homomorphism $\phi : S_1 \to B$ over $R$, the composition of $\phi$ with the multivariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_f$ equals the evaluation homomorphism $\text{aeval}_{\phi \circ f}$, where $f : \sigma \to S_1$ is a variable assignment. This expresses that applying $\phi$ after polynomial evaluation is equivalent to first composing $\phi$ with the variable assignment and then evaluating.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Composition with Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  (f : σ → S₁) {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] [inst_4 : Algebra R B] (φ : S₁ →ₐ[R] B) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.aeval f) p) = (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => φ (f i)) p
items.informal_description: For any $ R $-algebra homomorphism $ \varphi : S_1 \to B $ and polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, applying $ \varphi $ to the evaluation of $ p $ at a variable assignment $ f : \sigma \to S_1 $ equals the evaluation of $ p $ at the composed assignment $ \varphi \circ f $, i.e., $ \varphi(\text{aeval}_f(p)) = \text{aeval}_{\varphi \circ f}(p) $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Algebra Map and Evaluation Equals Original Homomorphism
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {S : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring A] [inst_3 : Algebra S R] [inst_4 : Algebra S A] (g : R →ₐ[S] A) (y : σ → A),
  (↑(MvPolynomial.aevalTower g y)).comp (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial σ R)) = ↑g
items.informal_description: The composition of the evaluation homomorphism $\text{aevalTower}_g(y)$ with the canonical algebra map from $R$ to the multivariate polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$ equals the original ring homomorphism $g$ from $R$ to $A$. This means that evaluating a polynomial whose coefficients are embedded via the algebra structure recovers the original homomorphism $g$.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Polynomial Evaluation with Ring Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] [inst_2 : Algebra R S₁]
  {B : Type u_2} [inst_3 : CommSemiring B] (g : σ → S₁) (φ : S₁ →+* B) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  φ ((MvPolynomial.aeval g) p) = (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (φ.comp (algebraMap R S₁)) fun i => φ (g i)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, commutative semiring $ S_1 $ with an $ R $-algebra structure, and commutative semiring $ B $, given a variable assignment $ g : \sigma \to S_1 $, a ring homomorphism $ \varphi : S_1 \to B $, and a polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, applying $ \varphi $ to the algebra evaluation $ \mathrm{aeval}_g(p) $ equals evaluating $ p $ using the composed ring homomorphism $ \varphi \circ \mathrm{algebraMap}_{R \to S_1} $ on coefficients and $ \varphi \circ g $ on variables. Symbolically, $ \varphi(\mathrm{aeval}_g(p)) = \mathrm{eval}_2^{\varphi \circ \mathrm{algebraMap}, \varphi \circ g}(p) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Multivariate Evaluation with Univariate Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  (f : σ → S) (i : σ), (MvPolynomial.aeval f).comp (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i) = Polynomial.aeval (f i)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to S $ and any index $ i \in \sigma $, the composition of the multivariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism $ \operatorname{aeval}_f $ with the univariate embedding $ \operatorname{toMvPolynomial}_i $ is equal to the univariate polynomial evaluation homomorphism at $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \operatorname{aeval}_f \circ \operatorname{toMvPolynomial}_i = \operatorname{aeval}(f(i)) $.
